words.prose: {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) makes the surah begin as commanded speech, not as an unframed report. The Form I 2ms imperative encodes a commissioned speaker while leaving the subject unspoken, then takes the whole following declaration, {{ar:هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ}} ({{tr:huwa Allāhu aḥadun}}), as its quoted complement; the local syntax fixes ayah 1 inside the quote, while wider surah-scope remains a discourse possibility rather than the forced local parse. The q-w-l field gives the command the weight of a transmitted statement and held doctrine, but the surface selects outward authorized saying, not inner thought, reciprocal disputation, or fabricated attribution. Its clipped weak-middle imperative form gives the opening a compressed launch before the fuller nominal clause. Variant openings without {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) show by contrast how much the standard verb contributes: the declaration is mediated as an utterance assigned to be voiced. The command also joins a familiar Quranic speech-about-God pattern while tightening it here around the unusual final singularity predicate.

topics.reason: Attachment evidence strongly marks {{ar:هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ}} ({{tr:huwa Allāhu aḥadun}}) as the quoted complement of {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) in ayah 1; claims that the syntax extends through the whole surah are therefore retained only as a broader discourse-scope possibility.

topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) as a Form I 2ms imperative with its subject encoded in the verb form, and the contextual profile marks this form-group as overwhelmingly imperative.

words.prose: {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) is the first word inside the commanded utterance, so the declaration begins with a pronoun before it gives the name. The attachment evidence preserves real ambiguity: it may introduce the whole matter as an affair-pronoun, point forward toward {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}), or answer an implied question; the point is not to collapse those options too early, because the reader has to move from pointer to named referent to predicate. As an independent 3ms word after the 2ms command, it shifts the speech from the commanded addressee to a third-person proposition and prevents the statement from being about the speaker. Its retained full word slot, tested by variants that omit it or preserve it without the command, makes the declaration more than a direct name-plus-predicate clause. The open vowels of {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) also create an audible bridge from the clipped command into the heavier divine name, and the recited boundary into {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) makes the pointer's attachment to its named referent audible.

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) is the named center of the quoted clause. If {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) is an affair-pronoun, the name begins the content clause; if the pronoun is referential, the name resolves it by apposition or first predicate. Either way, the word anchors the movement from pointer to final singularity. Its proper-name form keeps the referent fixed before {{ar:أَحَدٌ}} ({{tr:aḥadun}}) supplies the predicate, so the clause is not saying merely that some generic deity is one. The root-family pressures of worship, refuge, and bewildered awe remain useful around the name, especially because the pronoun briefly delays explicit naming, but local morphology keeps them subordinate to the proper noun. The word is not a Form V act of acquiring or performing divinity. Variant expansions and omissions show how compact the standard clause is: one name, one predicate, no removal of the command-pronoun frame, and no paired-title litany. The name also links the command to a broad Quranic speech-about-God pattern and then recurs immediately in the next ayah (112:2), where another predicate continues the same named anchor.

topics.headline: proper name fixes the referent

topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) as a definite proper noun with God as dominant referent in contextual profiles, so common-noun class readings must be excluded.

topics.headline: root-family pressure surrounds the name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that worship, refuge-seeking, and bewildered awe gather around the named identity, while the local word remains the proper name rather than a generic root-sense display.
topics.reason: No V4 guardrail rows are available for this root, and QAC marks the local surface as a proper noun; the etymological and disputed-root pressures survive as semantic atmosphere, not as activated replacement senses.

topics.headline: proper noun blocks acquired-divinity reading

topics.reason: The CRITICAL comparison with a derived Form V is useful only as contrast: the local form is the nominative proper noun {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}), not a derived verbal form.

topics.reason: The variant rows are retained as apparatus because they contrast the standard compact clause with openings that omit earlier framing or expand the name-plus-attribute sequence.

words.prose: {{ar:أَحَدٌ}} ({{tr:aḥadun}}) is the ayah's landing word. Its nominative tanwin and predicate position make singularity an asserted khabar of {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}), not an accusative state or a routine adjective after a definite name. The indefinite form gives the predicate open magnification, while its lexical contrast with {{ar:وَاحِد}} ({{tr:wāḥid}}) keeps the claim from meaning merely one item in a countable series: the force is indivisible uniqueness that admits no second. That force is distributionally marked because this form often lives in negative or scoped contexts, yet here it is affirmed of the divine name. The absence of a conjunction between name and predicate fuses identity and singularity, and the final position makes the word close the first ayah. Its recurrence in the surah's closing negation (112:4) answers the opening affirmation with denial of any equivalent, while the -ad sound links the first predicate to the next ayah's ending (112:2) and to the surah's audible closure system. Variant and expanded forms show the standard choice as compact: tanwin closes and magnifies the predicate rather than turning it into an enumerated pair of definite titles.

topics.headline: nominative form makes singularity predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that singularity is asserted as the clause's predicate, not added as a circumstantial state or ordinary adjective.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark {{ar:أَحَدٌ}} ({{tr:aḥadun}}) as nominative and as the khabar/predicate of the nominal clause, with definiteness mismatch against a routine adjective reading.

topics.headline: tanwin magnifies while closing the standard form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the tanwin keeps the predicate grammatically indefinite and expansive, while the standard recitation still closes ayah 1 before the next predicate begins.
topics.reason: QAC supports tanwin on {{ar:أَحَدٌ}} ({{tr:aḥadun}}) as significant for indefiniteness and grandeur; the no-tanwin variant is retained as boundary-sensitive apparatus, not as the governing standard parse.

topics.headline: aḥad excludes a countable second
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the predicate is not merely the number one but indivisible uniqueness that cannot be multiplied into two or many.
topics.reason: No V4 guardrail rows are available for this root, so the supplied lexical contrast with {{ar:وَاحِد}} ({{tr:wāḥid}}) is preserved as CRITICAL evidence while kept local to the singularity predicate rather than expanded into every root-family branch.

topics.headline: affirmative divine aḥad is marked
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a word often associated with negative or scoped anyone/no-one environments is here used as an affirmative divine predicate.
topics.reason: Contextual evidence marks this form as heavily negated/scoped and commonly generic-human in distribution, while the local clause predicates it affirmatively of {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}).

topics.headline: aḥad pairs tightly with name and command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the predicate is both adjacent to the divine name and inside the command-to-say frame, making the command-to-singularity relation especially tight.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL co-occurrence rows are supported locally by immediate adjacency in {{ar:ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ}} ({{tr:Allāhu aḥadun}}) and by the quote governed by {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}).

topics.headline: final asyndetic predicate resolves the clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause moves without a verb or conjunction from pronoun to name to final predicate, making singularity the point where the ayah comes to rest.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies a quoted nominal clause with {{ar:أَحَدٌ}} ({{tr:aḥadun}}) as predicate, and there is no conjunction between the name and predicate in the local surface.

topics.headline: opening affirmation returns as closing negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same singularity term affirmed in ayah 1 returns in the surah's closing denial of equivalence (112:4).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL echo rows explicitly link the affirmative {{ar:أَحَدٌ}} ({{tr:aḥadun}}) in 112:1 with its later negated recurrence in 112:4.

topics.headline: final sound binds the compact predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final -ad sound and the standard single predicate give compact audible closure instead of an expanded list of titles.
topics.reason: The local word closes ayah 1 as {{ar:أَحَدٌ}} ({{tr:aḥadun}}), while the variant and expanded forms are useful contrastive evidence for the standard's compactness and sound closure.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The command to say functions as a definition, not merely an utterance.** Lexical evidence: `ق و ل B001` (uttered speech), `ق و ل B016` (definition or essence stated as qawl), `ء ل ه B002`, `ء ح د B001` (absolute oneness), and later `ص م د B002` (compact solidity without hollowness). Structural cue: the imperative `قل` is followed by a pronoun, the repeated divine name, and a one-word predicate; 112:2 then gives another one-word predicate. Assigned roles: `قل` provides articulated form; `هو الله أحد` supplies the compressed definition; `الصمد` gives the defined One a dense, non-hollow support-image. Abductive move: I infer that the packet's extreme nominal compression makes the utterance definitional: the supplied words are not narrative events but essence-clauses. Reading change: 112:1 reads as "voice this boundary-definition of the referent" rather than simply "say a sentence about God."

2. **The speech corrects public attribution and circulating talk.** Lexical evidence: `ق و ل B005` (false saying or false attribution), `ق و ل B007` (circulating talk/public report), `و ل د B005` (generated/derived thing), `ك ف ء B001` (equal counterpart), and `ء ح د B002` in the final negated `أحد`. Structural cue: the positive command and declaration in 112:1 are followed by two negated clauses: no begetting/being begotten, no counterpart as anyone. Assigned roles: `قل` becomes the authorized counter-speech; the negated birth and counterpart clauses identify what kinds of wrong public saying are being fenced off. Abductive move: I supply the social-polemical arrow that an imperative to say a concise formula responds to possible claims in circulation; the packet supplies `ق و ل` and the subsequent denials. Reading change: 112:1 is not isolated affirmation; it is a corrective utterance that pre-empts derivative, filial, or equivalence attributions.

3. **The first `أحد` is sharpened by the last `أحد`: absolute one becomes no-anyone.** Lexical evidence: `ء ح د B001` in 112:1 (oneness and absolute one), `ء ح د B002` in 112:4 (negative exhaustive anyone), and `ك ف ء B001` (equal counterpart). Structural cue: the same surface-root appears at the opening assertion and closing negation; the first is indefinite affirmative predicate, the second indefinite under negation. Assigned roles: first `أحد` states uniqueness; final `أحد` scans the field of possible persons and exhausts it under "no counterpart." Abductive move: I infer that the closing negated use retroactively prevents the opening `أحد` from being read as merely numerical "one among countables." Reading change: 112:1 reads as absolute unshared singularity that has already excluded the possibility of a comparable "anyone."

4. **Oneness resists both rank-rivalry and peerhood.** Lexical evidence: `ء ح د B001/B005` (oneness; isolation), `س م و B007` (rivaling by vying upward) from the opening root inventory, `و ل د B006` (peer of the same birth-age), and `ك ف ء B001` (equal peer/counterpart). Structural cue: an initial raised name is followed by `أحد`, while later birth-based peerhood and counterpart equality are denied. Assigned roles: `أحد` marks non-participation in a competitive scale; `كفوًا` and `لدة`-like peerhood are the possible social/material equivalents refused by the surrounding ayat. Abductive move: I infer that if something is called one in a context saturated by name, birth, and equivalence, the local mechanism is not arithmetic but removal from rival classes. Reading change: `أحد` becomes solitude from rank competition, matching, and same-origin peerhood.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 112:4 most changed this ayah: the final `أحد` under negation made the first `أحد` feel less numerical and more like an assertion tested against an exhausted field of possible counterparts. 112:2 also surprised the reading of `قل`: because `الصمد` is so dense and predicate-like, the command to say became a command to state an essence-boundary. 112:3 corrected the social frame of the utterance by showing that the false attributions to be countered are not vague polytheistic plurality only, but specifically generation, derivation, parenthood, and peer-producing origin.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Speech made outward and repeatable.** Fixed-ayah `قُلْ` is directly anchored in `ق و ل:B001` (uttered speech), with latent `ق و ل:B007` supplying circulating public report in contrast to `ق و ل:B012`'s unspoken inner saying. The imperative form, followed by a compact declaration, structurally requires the thought to cross from inward conception into articulation; 112:0's `س م و:B005` designation gives that articulation a named referent. I infer from the imperative, not from an explicit audience marker, that the utterance is meant to be transmitted beyond the commanded speaker. The ayah therefore reads as the launching of a repeatable proclamation, not merely permission to hold a private belief.

2. **A commanded definition rather than a passing report.** The same fixed root offers `ق و ل:B016` (a definition or essence stated as qawl). After `قُلْ`, the packet presents two compact positive predicates in 112:1-2 and then paired exclusions in 112:3-4; `ٱللَّهُ` is also repeated as the subject at the opening of the first two positive statements. This sequence assigns the saying the role of setting a boundary around what the fixed designation can and cannot denote. The abductive move is that the ordered predicates and exclusions function together as a definition, although the packet never labels them as such. `قُلْ` consequently introduces a concise act of defining, not only the reporting of an isolated fact.

3. **The named subject as the destination of devotion and need.** Fixed-ayah `ٱللَّهُ` supports `ء ل ه:B001` (the worshipped one) as well as `ء ل ه:B002` (the fixed divine name). Its recurrence from 112:0 through 112:2 culminates in apposition with `ٱلصَّمَدُ`, whose `ص م د:B001` is the one intentionally resorted to and relied upon. The name identifies the subject, worship assigns the human orientation toward Him, and resort supplies the practical movement of needs in that same direction. I infer that devotion and dependence form one directional relation because the text juxtaposes their roots without explicitly stating the causal link. The clause thus reads `ٱللَّهُ` not as a bare proper name but as the uniquely named destination of worshipful reliance.

4. **Positive oneness completed by exhaustive exclusion.** Fixed-ayah `أَحَدٌ` directly activates `ء ح د:B001` (oneness and absolute one). The same surface returns at 112:4 inside `لَمْ ... أَحَدٌ`, where `ء ح د:B002` supplies exhaustive "anyone" under negation, and `ك ف ء:B001` names the equality being denied. The first occurrence establishes singular unity; the final occurrence tests the entire field for a matching member and finds none. The backward link is inferred from lexical repetition and the opening/closing placement. The first `أَحَدٌ` therefore reads as qualitative, unmatched oneness rather than merely the numeral one of `ء ح د:B003`.

5. **Unshared status, not disconnected solitude.** The fixed root's `ء ح د:B005` can activate isolation or being alone, and 112:3-4 initially sharpens that possibility by removing offspring and counterpart. Yet 112:0's `ر ح م:B001` establishes beneficent relation and 112:2's `ص م د:B001` establishes the approach of dependents. Those relations correct the isolation branch: I infer that relation can remain real without distributing the subject's status among peers. `أَحَدٌ` thus reads as unshared identity and rank, not as absence of care, address, or relational traffic.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 112:4's second `أَحَدٌ` was the decisive retrospective activation: its negative `ء ح د:B002` converted the first occurrence from possible numerical singularity into absolute oneness tested against every candidate for `ك ف ء:B001` equivalence. Meanwhile, 112:2's resort relation prevented dormant fixed `ء ح د:B005` from hardening into disconnected isolation, and the ordered predicates and exclusions of 112:2-4 made fixed `ق و ل:B016` visible as definition only after the full sequence had been read.

findings.text: Söyleme buyruğu, inancı içte tutulan bir düşünce olmaktan çıkarıp başkalarına aktarılabilen açık bir bildirime dönüştürür.
Bu söyleyiş, dolaşımdaki soy, türeme ve denklik yakıştırmalarını önceden karşılayan düzeltici bir söz işlevi görür.
Buyruktan sonra gelen kısa olumlu nitelemeler ve onları izleyen olumsuzlamalar, sözü geçici bir haberden çok sınırları çizilmiş bir tanıma dönüştürür.
Allah adı, sonraki dayanak niteliğiyle birlikte, ibadetin ve ihtiyacın aynı yönde toplandığı özneyi gösterir.
İlk ayetteki birlik, son ayette mümkün her dengi dışlayan kapsamlı olumsuzlamayla sınanır; böylece yalnızca sayısal bir birlik olmaktan çıkar.
Buradaki birlik, ilişkisiz bir yalnızlık değildir; merhamet ve kendisine yönelme ilişkileri sürerken Allah'ın kimliği ve konumu paylaşılmaz kalır.
Birlik, ortak kökenli akranların veya yükselme yarışındaki rakiplerin oluşturduğu bir sınıfa girmemeyi de bildirir.

butuncul_okuma_line.raw_line: **112:1.** قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ — Birincil okuma: Ayet, söylenmesi emredilen kısa bir tanım gibi işler: “O, Allah, birdir.” Sonraki “الصمد”, bu sözü yoğun ve içi boş olmayan bir öz-tanım hâline getirir; 112:3-4 ise bu birliği yalnız sayısal tekillik olmaktan çıkarıp türetilme, soy, rakiplik ve herhangi bir eş alanını kapatan kamusal bir düzeltmeye dönüştürür. {ق و ل B001; ق و ل B005; ق و ل B007; ق و ل B016; ء ل ه B002; ء ح د B001; ء ح د B002; ص م د B002; و ل د B005; ك ف ء B001}

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Absolute Oneness and Exhaustive Exclusion
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Positive singular identity is paired with negative quantification over every possible member of a class.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: absolute unity `ء ح د:B001/m01`; emphatic repeated one `ء ح د:B001/m02`; exhaustive negative “any one” `ء ح د:B002/m01`

In a negative frame, the same lexical field expands from one individual to anyone whatsoever, making singularity and exhaustive exclusion complementary operations.

branches.source_phrase_ar: أصل واحد وهو التعبد، فالإله الله تعالى لأنه معبود، وتأله الرجل إذا تعبد، والإلاهة الشمس سميت بذلك لأن قوما كانوا يعبدونها (maqayis)؛ التأله التعبد (ayn)؛ أله بالفتح إلاهة أي عبد عبادة، مألوه أي معبود، الآلهة الأصنام، التأليه التعبيد، التأله التنسك والتعبد (sihah)؛ لا يكون إلاها حتى يكون معبودا، معبوداتهم من الأصنام والأوثان آلهة، الإلاهة الشمس، وإلاهتك وعبادتك (tahdhib)؛ إله اسما لكل معبود، أله فلان يأله الآلهة عبد، فالإله على هذا هو المعبود (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi Yaratıcıya özgü adın kendisini, genel tapınılan-varlık adından türetiliş açıklamasını ve bu özel adla kurulan seslenme ile ant biçimlerini birlikte verir. Geçici çerçeve kullanılabilir, ancak dal yalnızca seslenme ve ant kalıpları değildir; özel adın yalın kullanımı da çekirdekte tutulmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın özel ad, doğrudan seslenme biçimleri ve ant ya da şaşma kalıpları ayrı tutulur; kalıplara özgü işlevler özel adın her kullanımına genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Yaratıcıya özgü adın kendisini ve bu adla kurulan seslenme, dilek, şaşma ve ant biçimlerini kapsar. Bu biçimler doğrudan seslenme, adın ant değeriyle kullanılması veya ses ve parçaların düşürülmesiyle kısaltılma yollarını gösterir.

facets.statement: Dalın merkezinde, Yaratıcıyı başkalarından ayırarak gösteren ve yalnız ona özgü sayılan özel ad bulunur.
Özel adın, tapınılan varlığı bildiren genel addan ses düşmesi ve belirleyici unsur eklenmesiyle oluştuğu açıklanır.
Özel ad, sözün başında ant değeri taşıyarak ardından gelen yapmama bildirimini güçlendirebilir.
Özel adın doğrudan ya da seslenme öğesi yerine geçen bir sonla kullanılması, yakarma ve dilek bildiren seslenme biçimleri kurar.
Ses veya parçaların düşürüldüğü kısalmış biçimler, şaşma ve ant anlatan kalıplarda kullanılır.
